newsitem.title: USA: US's Rubin--budget talks going well, no guarantees.
newsitem.headline: US's Rubin--budget talks going well, no guarantees.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said talks between the White House and Congress on balancing the budget were going well and that he was quite hopeful an agreement would be reached, but he added that there were no guarantees.

"I think that the budget talks are going well. There's been a very good atmosphere, a very constructive and I think positive atmosphere, around the talks, and I think I would be quite hopeful, but on the other hand there are no guarantees in life and we'll just have to see what happens," Rubin said.
The Treasury Secretary was speaking to Fox Television's Neil Cavuto in a taped interview to be aired in full at 1700 EDT/2100 GMT on Wednesday.
As for the U.S. dollar, Rubin reiterated that the Administration's policy on the dollar was unchanged. He added that he would not comment on the currency's near-term direction.

"If you're asking me what our policy is on the dollar, that is unchanged," Rubin said. "In terms of what the dollar is likely to do, that is a subject that I have restrained myself from commenting upon and will continue to do so."
Rubin also was asked what he is likely to do after President Bill Clinton leaves office after the new millennium.
"I truly don't know what I'll do when I'm finished with this," Rubin responded.

As for suggestions that he might succeed Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan, Rubin repeated that he is not interested in that position. "I've said before that's not what I'm interested in."
Commenting on the economy in general, the Treasury Secretary said the "most likely scenario" for the next year or so calls for continued growth with low inflation.
"(If) you look out some reasonable period of time, say look out a year ... the most likely scenario is a continuation of solid growth and low inflation.

"On the other hand, if you've been around for a while, which I have been, one of the lessons you learn, is you always need to be watchful with respect to inflation. So, while I do agree that inflation looks to me like it's likely to remain low, I also think we always have to be watchful," he added.
